data.one_liner: Client-agnostic network and WebSocket inspector for Flutter with overlay UI, replay, and MCP export
data.what_it_does: Intercepts and inspects HTTP and WebSocket traffic directly inside Flutter applications using an on-screen overlay UI. It offloads body parsing and serialization to background isolates and provides network simulation, HAR/cURL export, and Postman-style request replaying. It also exposes VM service extensions to connect with AI coding assistants via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
use_when: Debugging HTTP requests, GraphQL queries, or WebSocket frames directly on device or in simulators
Simulating offline or throttled network profiles (e.g., Slow 3G) inside your Flutter app
Inspecting app traffic using AI coding agents through Model Context Protocol (MCP)
avoid_when: Production builds where you do not want inspection overhead or potential data leakage
Apps looking for built-in HTTP client functionality without adding dedicated adapter packages
strengths: Client-agnostic design with modular adapters for Dio, http, Chopper, and WebSocket packages
Uses background isolates and hybrid storage to avoid UI frame drops on large payloads
Supports live bidirectional WebSocket frame inspection with ring-buffering and throttling
weaknesses: Requires installing and maintaining satellite adapter packages (e.g., interceptly_dio) to hook into client traffic
Documented platform support is currently limited to Android and iOS
data.setup_notes: Requires passing the app's NavigatorState GlobalKey to Interceptly.init and attaching the relevant adapter to your HTTP or WebSocket client.
